question: What is included in the initial static HTML shell when a route uses Partial Prerendering (PPR)?
options: Only the `<head>` tag; the entire `<body>` is always rendered on the client
All static components plus the `<Suspense fallback={...}>` UI for each dynamic component boundary
The resolved HTML of `cookies()` and `headers()` from the build server's environment
An empty HTML document that triggers a client-side `fetch()` for all Server Components
explanation: With Partial Prerendering, Next.js prerenders all static components along with the fallback UI of `<Suspense>` boundaries into the static shell, then streams the dynamic components at request time.

question: Why does calling `await cookies()` at the top of `Page()` and passing the value as a prop into `<Suspense><UserBanner cookie={val} /></Suspense>` prevent prerendering the page shell?
options: Because props passed across a `<Suspense>` boundary cannot be strings
Because `await cookies()` executes inside `Page()` before `Page()` returns its JSX, above the `<Suspense>` boundary
Because `cookies()` can only be called inside Client Components
Because `<Suspense>` boundaries only work with `headers()`, not `cookies()`
explanation: A `<Suspense>` boundary only catches asynchronous suspensions that occur inside its children. If `Page()` awaits `cookies()` before returning JSX, `Page()` itself suspends outside of any `<Suspense>` boundary.

question: How should you refactor a layout that reads a session cookie to show a user avatar so that the layout shell remains static?
options: Move the `await cookies()` call into a child `<UserAvatar />` Server Component and wrap `<UserAvatar />` in `<Suspense>` inside the layout
Keep `await cookies()` in the layout but wrap the layout's `children` prop in `<Suspense>`
Convert the entire `RootLayout` into a Client Component with `'use client'`
Call `cookies()` without `await` so that it executes synchronously at build time
explanation: By moving `await cookies()` into `<UserAvatar />` and wrapping `<UserAvatar />` in `<Suspense fallback={<AvatarSkeleton />}>`, the layout itself does not block on request data and can be statically prerendered.

question: When multiple dynamic `<Suspense>` holes exist on the same page in Partial Prerendering, how are they resolved at request time?
options: In separate HTTP requests initiated one by one after hydration completes
Concurrently on the server, streaming each resolved chunk in the same HTTP response as soon as it finishes
Strictly sequentially from top to bottom of the DOM tree, waiting for each hole before starting the next
Only the first `<Suspense>` hole is streamed; remaining holes fall back to client-side rendering
explanation: Next.js executes dynamic Server Component subtrees in parallel on the server and streams their HTML chunks over the same initial HTTP connection as each `<Suspense>` boundary resolves.
